transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I've been having this issue with eating lately. Some evenings after work, especially on days where I've been really strict about what I eat all day, I just... I end up eating way more than I meant to. It's like I'll have dinner, and then I'll have a bowl of cereal, and then crackers, and then whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets... all just packed into a couple of hours. It's just getting to be a bit much.
When this happens, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah, exactly. Once I get started on those nights, it's like... I just keep going back to the kitchen. Even while I'm actively telling myself to stop, I just can't seem to listen. I don't really feel back in charge of myself until I'm uncomfortably full.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo them?
No, I don't do that. I've never tried to make myself throw up or anything like that. I just... I mostly just deal with feeling overly full and guilty about it, but no, I don't make myself sick.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate by exercising a lot?

Yeah, I do. The next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I'm making up for it. I'll usually skip breakfast and lunch... or I'll go take an extra-long hike. Sometimes I'll just push myself a lot harder at my softball conditioning, even when I'm really tired. I just feel like I have to do something to balance it out.
Are you currently at a body weight that is much lower than what would be expected for your height?
No, I wouldn't say so. My weight is... it's pretty normal for my height, really. I'm definitely not underweight or anything like that.
Are you very afraid of gaining weight?

No, not really. I mean, I'd prefer not to gain weight, obviously, but I wouldn't say I'm terrified of it. I don't really obsess over the scale or anything like that. It's more just about how uncomfortable and guilty I feel after I eat too much, rather than a huge fear of gaining weight.
After these overeating episodes, do you usually do something to try to make up for them?

Well, just like I mentioned a minute ago, yeah. I'll usually skip breakfast and lunch the next day, or I'll push myself to go on a really long hike. I just do those things I brought up earlier to try and balance it out. But I don't really do anything else besides that, if that's what you mean.
About how often do these overeating episodes happen?

Well, for the past few months, it's been happening most weeks. Usually, there's one or two nights a week where I end up eating way more than I planned to. And then, like I said, the next day I try to make up for it by skipping my meals or going on a longer hike to exercise it off.
On average, how often do you skip meals or exercise extra to make up for these eating episodes?

Yeah, I guess it's pretty much exactly what I just mentioned, since it goes right along with the eating. So, for the past few months, it's been most weeks. Whenever I have one of those one or two nights where I eat far more than I planned, the very next day is when I try to make up for it by skipping my meals or exercising longer. So, on average, I'd say about once or twice a week.
During these episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food for the situation?

Yeah, I do. It's actually a big part of what brought me in to see you. Some evenings after work, especially when I've been really strict with my eating all day, I just end up eating way more than I ever meant to. I'll sit down and have my dinner, but then... I'll just keep going. I'll have a bowl of cereal, some crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets on top of that. And it's all just within a couple of hours.
